area.title: Notification type and origin of the import
area.scope: Starting a notification (create-notification, the DR2.1 notification type question, the reference given to a new notification) and the origin of the import page: country of origin and its list, the region of origin code question and prefix, the internal reference, their saving, validation and exits; the countries reference list and the reference-data service mechanics behind it. Stops at what-are-you-importing (commodities). Includes the high-risk plants frontend's origin page and its origin rulings (plants starts on the commodity type, so plants has no notification type question).

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.
claims.quote: Now we need to be really careful here because the prototype isn't accessible. It's not using some GDS stuff. It's using prototype thrown up by AI stuff. ... the prototype isn't necessarily production-grade with its solution.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled

claims.statement: The service serves the list of countries at GET /countries.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/countries")

claims.statement: GET /countries takes one optional query parameter, blocks.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(required = false, value = "blocks") String blocks

claims.statement: GET /countries returns 200 with a JSON array of countries.
claims.quote: return ResponseEntity.ok(countries);

claims.statement: GET /countries returns countries sorted by their name.
claims.quote: .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Country::getName))

claims.statement: The country sort is a plain case-sensitive string comparison of the name, not a locale-aware collation, so names are ordered by character code.
claims.quote: Comparator.comparing(Country::getName)
claims.note: Comparator.comparing on a String uses String.compareTo; no Collator is applied.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom (effectiveAlpha2 GB) is always removed from the countries list, whatever blocks value is asked for.
claims.quote: .filter(c -> !"GB".equals(c.getEffectiveAlpha2()))

claims.statement: When blocks is given, a country is kept only if one of its MDM blocks has a name equal to the blocks value and includeCountry true.
When blocks is not given, no block filter is applied and every country except the United Kingdom is returned.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: When blocks is given but MDM sends a country with no blocks list at all, that country is kept rather than filtered out.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: The blocks value is also passed to MDM as its own blocks query parameter, so MDM filters first and the service filters again on includeCountry.
claims.quote: mdmClient.getCountries(ocpApimSubscriptionKey, SYSTEM, blocks);

claims.statement: The block filter compares the whole blocks value with a single block name, so asking for several blocks at once in one value (for example comma-separated) would match no country unless MDM names a block that way.
claims.quote: requestedBlock.equals(b.getName())
claims.note: No splitting of the blocks value is done anywhere in the service.

claims.statement: The block names used in tests are GBNAG_SPS_EX, GBNAG_PHYTO_EX and OMR; the service has no fixed list of allowed block values and accepts any string.
claims.quote: restTemplate.getForEntity("/countries?blocks=GBNAG_PHYTO_EX", String.class);
claims.note: No validation of the blocks parameter exists in the controller or service.

claims.statement: Each returned country has a code field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlpha2 (the ISO alpha-2 code).
claims.quote: this.code = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlpha2();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a name field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlias (the short display name, such as "United Kingdom"), not MDM's name or longName.
claims.quote: this.name = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlias();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a subDivisions field: a list of its subdivisions, and an empty list when MDM sends none or a null list.
claims.quote:
if (mdmSubDivisions == null || mdmSubDivisions.isEmpty()) {
      return List.of();

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a code field taken from MDM's code.value (such as ES-CN).
claims.quote: .code(subDivision.getCode().getValue())

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a name field taken from MDM's subdivision name (such as Canary Islands).
claims.quote: .name(subDivision.getName())

claims.statement: A subdivision MDM sends with no code, or a code with no value, is dropped from the country's subdivisions.
claims.quote:
.filter(subDivision -> subDivision.getCode() != null
            && subDivision.getCode().getValue() != null)

claims.statement: Subdivisions are returned in the order MDM sends them; they are not sorted.
claims.quote: return mdmSubDivisions.stream()
claims.note: No sort is applied in mapSubDivisions or anywhere else to subdivisions.

claims.statement: A country is returned with only code, name and subDivisions: MDM's longName, name, independent, statusName, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, systemLongName, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveLongName and blocks are all dropped.
An MDM subdivision's blocs list is dropped; a subdivision is returned with only code and name.
claims.quote: private List<String> blocs;

claims.statement: MDM's block records carry name, includeCountry and tags; tags are read but never used.
A subdivision code arrives from MDM wrapped in an object with a single value field.
claims.quote: "code": { "value": "FR-MQ" }

claims.statement: When MDM returns no countries, GET /countries returns 200 with an empty array.
claims.quote:
assertThat(response.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.OK);
    assertThat(response.getBody()).isEmpty();

claims.statement: When MDM answers the countries call with an empty body, the service treats it as no countries and returns an empty list rather than an error.
A country with no name would make the sort fail, so GET /countries would answer 500 if MDM sent a country with no effectiveAlias.
claims.quote: .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Country::getName))
claims.note: Comparator.comparing without nullsFirst/nullsLast throws NullPointerException on a null key, which the RuntimeException handler maps to 500. Not tested.

claims.statement: Countries are read from MDM's geography countries list (/mdm/geo/countries).
claims.quote: @GetMapping(value = "/mdm/geo/countries")

claims.statement: Every MDM call asks for the GBNAG system's view of the list.
claims.quote: private static final String SYSTEM = "GBNAG";

claims.statement: Every MDM call carries the platform subscription key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header, read from configuration.
claims.quote: ocpApimSubscriptionKey: ${TRADE_PLATFORM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY:[REDACTED]}

claims.statement: Every MDM call carries a bearer token obtained from the trade platform's OAuth token endpoint with the client-credentials grant.
claims.quote: formData.add("grant_type", "client_credentials");

claims.statement: The bearer token is reused until its expiresOn time passes; a token with no expiresOn is treated as already expired, so a new one is fetched on the next call.
The MDM base URL is set by MDM_SERVICE_URL and defaults to http://localhost:8087 (the local stub).
claims.quote: url: ${MDM_SERVICE_URL:http://localhost:8087}

claims.statement: MDM and trade-auth calls are configured with a 3000 ms connection timeout and a 3000 ms read timeout.
claims.quote:
connectionTimeout: 3000
  readTimeout: 3000
claims.note: Whether these values are wired into the Feign clients is not shown in this part's files; MdmConfiguration only holds them.

claims.statement: The service logs MDM's x-ms-middleware-request-id trace header for each call, and a missing header only logs a warning; the list is still returned.
claims.quote: log.warn("No MDM trace id returned");

claims.statement: Countries returned by MDM are cached in memory in MDM_COUNTRIES_CACHE, keyed by the blocks value, so each distinct blocks value (including none) is fetched and cached separately.
claims.quote:
@Cacheable(value = "MDM_COUNTRIES_CACHE", unless = "#result == null || #result.isEmpty()")
  public List<MdmCountry> getCountries(String blocks) {

claims.statement: Ports of entry returned by MDM are cached in memory in MDM_POE_CACHE.
claims.quote: @Cacheable(value = "MDM_POE_CACHE", unless = "#result == null || #result.isEmpty()")

claims.statement: An empty list from MDM is never cached, for countries or ports, so the next request calls MDM again.
claims.quote: unless = "#result == null || #result.isEmpty()"

claims.statement: A countries result that is empty only because every country was filtered out (for example by the block filter) is also not cached.
claims.note: The cache condition is applied to the filtered result the method returns.

claims.statement: Both MDM caches expire entries a set number of minutes after they are written, set by CACHE_MDM_TTL_MINUTES and defaulting to 60 minutes.
claims.quote: ttl-minutes: ${CACHE_MDM_TTL_MINUTES:60}

claims.statement: Each MDM cache holds at most 20 entries.
claims.quote: .maximumSize(20)

claims.statement: The caches exist to limit how often the service calls MDM, not to survive MDM being down or to speed responses up.
claims.quote:
// The primary purpose of caching MDM responses is to rate-limit our calls to MDM,
        // rather than to defend against MDM unavailability or improve performance.

claims.statement: The service also registers an IDENTITY_TOKEN_CACHE (at most 5 entries, 30-minute expiry), which no list endpoint uses.
claims.quote: new CaffeineCacheManager("IDENTITY_TOKEN_CACHE");
claims.note: No @Cacheable in the read files names IDENTITY_TOKEN_CACHE; the MDM token is held inside the interceptor instead.

claims.statement: The service listens on port 8086 by default.
claims.quote: port: ${PORT:8086}

claims.statement: Any unexpected runtime error, including a failed MDM call, is answered with 500 and an RFC 7807 problem body titled "Internal Server Error" with detail "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later." and type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/internal-error.
claims.quote: "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."
claims.note: That a failed MDM call lands here is inferred: Feign errors are RuntimeExceptions and nothing else catches them. The lists have no fallback to stale data.

claims.statement: A NotFoundException is answered with 404, title "Resource Not Found", the exception's message as detail and type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found; neither list endpoint throws it.
claims.quote: problemDetail.setTitle("Resource Not Found");

claims.statement: A ConflictException is answered with 409, title "Resource Conflict", the exception's message as detail and type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/conflict; neither list endpoint throws it.
claims.quote: problemDetail.setTitle("Resource Conflict");

claims.statement: A request-body validation failure is answered with 400, title "Validation Error", detail "Validation failed for one or more fields", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/validation-error and an errors map of field to message; neither list endpoint takes a validated body, so the lists never return it.
claims.quote: "Validation failed for one or more fields"

claims.statement: Every error body carries a traceId property with the request's trace id when one is set, and omits it otherwise.
claims.quote:
if (traceId != null) {
      problemDetail.setProperty("traceId", traceId);

claims.statement: Spring's own errors, such as 404 for an unknown path, are left to Spring and not reshaped by the handler.
claims.quote:
Note: Does NOT catch Spring framework exceptions like NoResourceFoundException (404) or other
   * HTTP-related exceptions.

claims.statement: TradeImportsReferenceDataException is documented as mapping to 404 but has no handler of its own, so if thrown it would be answered as a 500.
claims.quote: Will be mapped to 404 Not Found by GlobalExceptionHandler.
claims.note: It extends RuntimeException and GlobalExceptionHandler has no @ExceptionHandler for it; nothing in the read files throws it.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/geo/countries, standing in for MDM's countries reference-data call.
claims.quote: @GetMapping(value = "/mdm/geo/countries")

claims.statement: The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header; Spring rejects a request without it, so a call with no key is refused (a bad request) rather than answered.
claims.note: The header is required by default (@RequestHeader with no required=false). The 400 outcome is Spring's default for a missing required header, not code in the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts any subscription-key value: the key is read but never checked, so any non-empty value gets the full answer.
claims.quote: @RequestHeader(OCP_APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY) String ocpApimSubscriptionKey,
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses ocpApimSubscriptionKey.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional system query parameter but ignores it: the same list comes back whatever system is asked for.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(value = "system", required = false) String system,
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses system.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional blocks query parameter but does not filter on it: every call returns the whole fixture, whichever block is asked for or if none is.
claims.note: Inferred because blocks is never read in the method body. Outside this slice, trade-imports-reference-data's MdmService passes system GBNAG and blocks to MDM and then filters the answer by block itself (isIncludedInRequestedBlock), so on the stack the filtering a user sees is done by reference-data, not by the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint answers 200 OK with a JSON array of country records read from responses/countriesResponse.json.
The countries endpoint sets the response header x-ms-middleware-request-id to the fixed value stub-trace-id.

A country's block membership is a record of the block name, an includeCountry boolean and a list of string tags.
A subdivision record carries a code (an object holding a single value string), a name and a list of blocs (spelt blocs, not blocks).

claims.statement: By default the MDM paths answer with no added delay (profile zero-delay), and the interim service-level targets are p50 100 ms, p95 400 ms and p99 1,000 ms, recorded as not agreed.
claims.note: The latency profiles themselves are out of scope; this claim records only what the block says for the two MDM paths.

claims.statement: The README says the stub stands in for MDM reference data through APIM, which trade-imports-reference-data calls, on GET /mdm/geo/countries and GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.

This stub stands in for two integrations that `trade-imports-reference-data` calls, and gives each its own latency profile:
...
| `mdm` | MDM reference data through APIM | `GET /mdm/geo/countries`, `GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes` |

claims.quote: | `mdm` | `GET /mdm/geo/countries`, `GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes` |
claims.note: The fault kinds and controls are out of scope.

claims.statement: The stub has no block other than GBNAG_SPS_EX and ignores the blocks parameter, so it cannot offer a germinal-products country list, or any list that differs between the live-animals and germinal-products journeys, on the local stack.
claims.note: Looked for any other block name in the fixture with jq and for any blocks handling in the controller; there is none. Whether germinal products need a different block is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: The countries fixture offers no country outside the EU and EFTA, so a live-animals or germinal-products notification from a non-European country of origin cannot be made against the stub.
claims.note: Looked at all 31 country records. Whether the journeys need non-European origins is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: Subdivisions carry no region or block data in the fixture, so the stub cannot show whether a region such as the Canary Islands or Madeira is treated differently from its country for live animals or germinal products.
claims.note: Looked at all nine subdivision entries; none sets blocs. Whether the journeys need region-level origin is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: The fixture gives Reunion the subdivision code FR-LRE and spells the name without its accent; FR-LRE is not the ISO 3166-2 form the other French codes follow (two letters after FR-, such as FR-MQ or FR-GP), so a page or mapping keyed on ISO subdivision codes would not match Reunion from the stub.
claims.note: Inferred from the pattern of the five other French subdivision codes in the same list; whether live MDM also uses FR-LRE is not knowable from the stub.

claims.statement: The README says trade-imports-reference-data calls the Trade Platform OAuth token endpoint before MDM, and the stub answers that too, on POST /tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token, as a separate integration with its own latency profile.
claims.quote: | `trade-token` | The Trade Platform OAuth token endpoint, called before MDM | `POST /tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token` |
claims.note: Not an MDM row itself, but it is how the MDM calls are reached; the token stub's own behaviour is outside this part.

claims.statement: The origin page shows the caption 'About the consignment', the heading 'Origin of the import', and a strip with a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification reference.
claims.quote:
Draft GBN-AG-26-D2F0S1 ... About the consignment

Origin of the import
claims.note: Context only; the origin page's other fields and buttons are another part's slice.

claims.statement: The type-ahead uses the third-party accessible-autocomplete component (autocomplete__* classes and its own stylesheet rules), which sits outside govuk-frontend; the service wraps it in its own module, app-accessible-autocomplete, and restyles it to match GOV.UK inputs.
claims.ref: trace bd485 frame snapshot call@4165 (autocomplete__wrapper, data-module app-accessible-autocomplete); stylesheet application.f6b50c7.min.css autocomplete__* rules
claims.quote: "data-module":"app-accessible-autocomplete"
claims.note: Inferred from the non-govuk class names and the custom data-module name. accessible-autocomplete is the alphagov component GOV.UK services commonly use for this pattern; no govuk-frontend component replaces it.

claims.statement: The country list reaches the page server-side: no browser request for country data appears in any trace's network log, only the page HTML, stylesheet, script and crest.
claims.ref: trace bd485 1-trace.network (all requests); same pattern in the other nine traces
claims.quote: GET	200	http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-D2F0S1/origin
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any data call; the type-ahead filters the options already in the select.

claims.statement: The source the 40-country list is read from (the spec calls it MDM) is never seen: no trace shows the server's call for country reference data, its shape, or what happens if it fails.
claims.ref: all 10 traces, network logs; spec origin.fit.spec.js test 'renders the captured MDM country options and feature copy' (outside this slice)

claims.statement: Keyboard use of the list is not exercised: no trace presses the up or down arrow keys, Enter or Tab to review or choose a country, although the assistive hint promises arrow-key and Enter support.
No trace shows what happens when the user types text and leaves the box without choosing an option (blur, Escape, or submitting a partial name): whether the text is cleared, kept, or matched.
claims.note: The type-ahead is configured with data-auto-select="false", so a typed match is not chosen for the user.

claims.statement: The text announced through the live regions (for example how many results are available) is never captured: both status regions are empty in every snapshot taken.
No trace in this slice shows the type-ahead, with JavaScript on, opening on a notification that already has a saved country: whether the saved country's name appears in the box is not shown here.
claims.ref: all 10 traces; only 0141f revisits a saved origin page, with JavaScript off
claims.note: data-default-value is empty on a new notification; the saved-value case may be covered by another part's origin traces.

claims.statement: The error state without JavaScript (the plain select with an error) is not traced; only the enhanced input's error border is shown.
claims.ref: trace 0141f (no-JS, happy path only); trace f489f (JS on)
claims.note: The server HTML in f489f shows the select itself gets govuk-select--error, which would be what a no-JavaScript user sees, but no trace renders it with JavaScript off.

claims.statement: The type-ahead is only exercised at a 1280x720 desktop viewport; its look and the 16px small-screen font size the stylesheet defines below 641px are not shown on a narrow screen.
The origin form is a POST form with browser validation turned off (novalidate), so every origin rule is checked on the server.

sources.role: how the real services behave end to end today

claims.statement: Starting a new notification from the dashboard creates it with a POST and sends the user straight to the origin page of the new notification: Origin of the import is the first page of the journey.

claims.quote: POST /live-animals/notifications 302 /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-QA45SC/origin

claims.statement: Each new notification is given a reference of the form GBN-AG-26- followed by six letters and digits when it is created, and the reference is part of every journey URL.

claims.quote: GBN-AG-26-QA45SC
claims.note: Other references seen: GBN-AG-26-R42PJ0, GBN-AG-26-TAG440, GBN-AG-26-GTFZAB, GBN-AG-26-RD5XQF, GBN-AG-26-G3RH4A, GBN-AG-26-9ZZGJS, GBN-AG-26-6H01GG.

claims.quote: Draft GBN-AG-26-QA45SC
claims.note: The strip is the non-govuk class app-journey-strip around a govuk-tag--blue and a bold govuk-body span. The visual spec masks it because the reference changes every run.

claims.statement: The origin page has the caption 'About the consignment' above its heading.

claims.statement: On the first visit to the origin page, straight after starting a notification, the Back link goes to the dashboard; on a later visit from the overview it goes to the notification overview.
claims.ref: trace T01 action call@288 (back href /live-animals) and call@314, call@358 (back href /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-QA45SC)
claims.quote: Back

claims.statement: The origin page asks for the country of origin, labelled 'Country of origin' as a medium label.
claims.quote: Country of origin

claims.statement: The country of origin field has the hint 'Start typing to search for a country.'
claims.quote: Start typing to search for a country.

claims.statement: With JavaScript on, the country of origin is a type-ahead combobox whose accessible name is 'Country of origin'; it enhances a native select that stays in the page.
claims.ref: trace T01 actions call@318 (to.have.role combobox) and call@320 (to.have.accessible.name Country of origin); call@288 DOM shows input#countryOfOrigin role=combobox beside select#countryOfOrigin-select

claims.statement: The native country select is the no-JavaScript fallback and is what carries the submitted value: before enhancement the server renders it as a plain select with id countryOfOrigin.
claims.ref: trace T01 action call@314 (server-rendered DOM before the script ran) and features/country-of-origin-type-ahead.spec.ts comment
claims.quote: The select stays in the DOM as the no-JavaScript fallback and is what carries the code the form submits
claims.note: No trace runs with JavaScript off, so the fallback itself is never driven.

claims.statement: The country of origin list holds 41 options: the placeholder 'Select a country' first, then 40 places in alphabetical order.
claims.ref: trace T01 actions call@322 (first option has text Select a country) and call@324 (option count 41)
claims.quote: Select a country

claims.statement: The 40 places offered as country of origin, with the code each submits, are: Austria AT, Azores PT-20, Belgium BE, Bulgaria BG, Canary Islands ES-CN, Croatia HR, Cyprus CY, Czechia CZ, Denmark DK, Estonia EE, Finland FI, France FR, French Guiana FR-GF, Germany DE, Greece GR, Guadeloupe FR-GP, Hungary HU, Iceland IS, Ireland IE, Italy IT, Latvia LV, Liechtenstein LI, Lithuania LT, Luxembourg LU, Madeira PT-30, Malta MT, Martinique FR-MQ, Mayotte FR-YT, Netherlands (the) NL, Norway NO, Poland PL, Portugal PT, Reunion FR-LRE, Romania RO, Saint Martin (French part) FR-MF, Slovakia SK, Slovenia SI, Spain ES, Sweden SE, Switzerland CH.

claims.note: The spec calls these 'the 31 SPS origin countries and nine journey subdivisions'.

claims.statement: Nine of the country of origin entries are subdivisions rather than countries, and they submit subdivision codes: Azores PT-20, Canary Islands ES-CN, French Guiana FR-GF, Guadeloupe FR-GP, Madeira PT-30, Martinique FR-MQ, Mayotte FR-YT, Reunion FR-LRE and Saint Martin (French part) FR-MF. claims.quote: The scroll-only divider rule is gone — a searchable list has no use for it.

claims.statement: Focusing the country of origin field opens the whole list of 40 places before anything is typed.

claims.quote: aria-setsize="40"
claims.note: The select carries data-min-length="0" data-show-all-values="true".

claims.ref: trace T01 actions call@328 (fill Belg) and call@330 (option Belgium visible)
claims.quote: fill #countryOfOrigin Belg

claims.ref: trace T01 actions call@344, call@346 (#countryOfOrigin has value Belgium) and call@348 (select has value BE)
claims.quote: expect select[name="countryOfOrigin"] to.have.value BE

claims.statement: The origin form submits the country of origin as its code in the field countryOfOrigin, not as the name.
claims.ref: trace T01 request POST /origin (second save); T15 request POST /origin
claims.quote: countryOfOrigin=BE
claims.note: T15 submits countryOfOrigin=ES-CN for Canary Islands.

claims.statement: A saved country of origin is shown again on return: the select holds the code and the chosen name sits visibly in the search box.
claims.ref: trace T01 actions call@358 (select value BE) and call@360 (#countryOfOrigin value Belgium)
claims.quote: The chosen country is left sitting visibly in the search box on return.

claims.ref: trace T15 actions call@1094 (select value ES-CN) and call@1096 (#countryOfOrigin value Canary Islands)
claims.quote: expect #countryOfOrigin to.have.value Canary Islands

claims.quote: When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select.  Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures.

claims.statement: The country and port type-aheads are built with the accessible-autocomplete component (autocomplete__* classes, a service module app-accessible-autocomplete) rather than a govuk-frontend component; govuk-frontend has no type-ahead of its own.
claims.ref: trace T01 action call@288 and T02 action call@629, autocomplete__wrapper / autocomplete__input / autocomplete__menu classes and data-module="app-accessible-autocomplete"

claims.quote: If a region of origin code is required it will be shown on your health certificate.

claims.quote: Enter up to 5 characters.

claims.quote: Error: Enter the region of origin code

claims.quote: <input class="govuk-input govuk-input--width-5" id="regionOfOriginCodeSuffix" name="regionOfOriginCodeSuffix" type="text" value="75"
